A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Concrete Score Distillation work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and expanded material.

before.justification: V1 reports original teacher–student distillation experiments, instruction-following and task-specific results, weighting ablations, and generation examples in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds general-chat evaluations, calibration and gradient analyses, adaptive-weighting experiments, and computational resource measurements.

M1.justification: The core pairwise logit objective, analytic gradient procedure, and reference implementation remain unchanged. Appendix D.2 introduces tested adaptive weighting variants: geometric interpolation between student and teacher probabilities controlled by two epoch schedules or a token-specific entropy rule.

E1.justification: V2 adds general-chat distillation using 50,000 UltraChat prompts and evaluation on MT-Bench and AlpacaEval (Sections 4.3 and C.3). The existing instruction-following, dialogue summarization, low-resource translation, and arithmetic-reasoning coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds DLD comparators within the retained on-policy and task-specific experiments, including centered and standardized variants (Tables 2, 3, 5, and 10). It newly evaluates DPKD and DistiLLM-2 in Table 4 and extends the probability-loss comparison to weighted KL, TV, and SRKL in Table 8.

E3.justification: New protocols include Qwen2.5-7B-to-1.5B and Gemma2-9B-to-2B distillation using teacher/student-generated responses, GPT-4/GPT-4-Turbo judging, and AlpacaEval win rates against text-davinci-003. V2 also introduces calibration measurements and a separately specified single-A100 efficiency comparison. Existing Dolly and task-specific settings are largely retained and relocated into Appendix C.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's weighting, decoding-temperature, offset, and Monte Carlo analyses, v2 tests normalized DLD variants and weighting-temperature sensitivity. It adds calibration comparisons, offset dynamics during training, adaptive weighting, gradient-coefficient entropy, and a DLD generation-failure example (Section 4.4 and Appendix D).

E5.justification: V2 adds standard deviations to existing weighting-ablation results in Tables 5 and 8, corresponding to v1 Tables 4 and 6. Both versions already specify the same five evaluation seeds; the additional uncertainty reporting does not establish an increase in training runs.

E6.justification: Many chat, calibration, efficiency, and ablation results are added, while retained scores in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. New DistiLLM+DLD achieves 17.69 on GPT-2-0.1B Vicuna Eval versus the best CSD score of 17.18, changing the expanded comparison's winner. Table 4 reports Qwen MT-Bench/GPT-4 scores of 7.69 for CSD(S,S) versus 7.28 for DistiLLM-2. Probability-L2 U/S result assignments also swap: their averages change from 11.35/11.13 in v1 Table 6 to 11.13/11.35 in v2 Table 8.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds mathematical definitions of normalized DLD variants and Remark 4's weighted-centering equivalence argument. Appendix A.5 newly derives how weighted KL changes the target distribution. Proposition 1 and Theorem 2 replace the sufficient-capacity wording with an explicit infinite-capacity assumption; their underlying proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed demonstrated applicability to general-chat distillation with Qwen2.5 and Gemma2, including a 9B teacher. The central claims concerning shift invariance, linear-time computation, flexible weighting, and fidelity–diversity trade-offs remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly reports and interprets CSD(S,S) failure under limited-data task-specific distillation, motivating teacher–student weighting through calibration. It adds explanations linking uniform weighting to minority-vocabulary learning and high-temperature performance, and explains adaptive weighting behavior. Sections 3.2 and 4.4 also qualify Monte Carlo's convergence disadvantage and discuss its broader modeling flexibility.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code repository link, explicit Monte Carlo pseudocode in Algorithm 2, and general-chat implementation information. Table 9 newly documents profiling configurations, including sequence limits, LoRA use, microbatch/accumulation settings, A100 hardware, and resource costs. The original code snippet and existing training details are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds AMid and a subsection distinguishing CSD from BPO's sequence-level preference matching and ARD's diffusion-to-autoregressive distillation. References also add logit standardization and works supporting the new chat experiments. The original positioning as a logit-level alternative to f-divergence objectives remains.

P1.justification: Existing experimental setup and evaluation descriptions are consolidated into Appendix C.1–C.2, with shorter main-text summaries. Related work and supplementary analyses gain subheadings; the abstract is edited, and conference headers and acknowledgments are added. Most introduction, method, and conclusion prose is retained.

P2.justification: Several comparison tables are substantially expanded, and new chat, calibration, efficiency, and task-specific tables are added. Figure 5 becomes a three-panel display; v1's two-panel offset Figure 8 becomes v2's four-panel Figure 9. New Figures 10–13 present additional analyses, while v1's training-curve Figure 9 is retained as v2 Figure 8.

improvement.justification: The added shift-aware DLD controls, Qwen2.5/Gemma2 chat evaluations, and disclosure of CSD(S,S) failure substantially strengthen empirical assessment and guidance on weighting choices. Mechanism analyses and reproducibility information address important gaps in v1. These gains outweigh localized inconsistencies: Table 2 no longer supports the retained claim of winning every benchmark, and Remark 4's exact gradient equality misses a factor of two under Equation 8's normalization.
